summary.text: Pamelya Herndon is a Democratic state representative from District 28 who has represented the district since 2021 and is seeking re-election in the New Mexico House of Representatives in the November 3, 2026 general election.
Herndon is an attorney who was appointed to the seat by the Bernalillo County Commission in June 2021 and later won election to it.

paragraphs.text: Pamelya Herndon graduated from Roy Miller High School, earned a bachelor's degree in accounting from Howard University in 1975 and a J.D. from the University of Texas in 1978.
In a Ballotpedia survey, she said she holds law licenses in New Mexico and Colorado and is a licensed Certified Public Accountant in Texas.

She said she began her career as an estate tax attorney for the Internal Revenue Service and later became a senior trial attorney in the IRS Office of District Counsel, and that she has served as an assistant attorney general for New Mexico, general counsel for the Regulation and Licensing Department and deputy cabinet secretary of the General Services Department.

Ballotpedia also lists her as president and CEO of KWH Law Center for Social Justice and Change, executive director of the Southwest Women's Law Center and first vice president of the NAACP Albuquerque Branch.
The Bernalillo County Commission appointed Herndon to the state House on June 22, 2021, to replace Melanie Stansbury, who had been elected to Congress.
She won the District 28 seat in the 2022 and 2024 elections, according to her survey responses, and Ballotpedia reports that she defeated Marcie May in the November 2024 general election.
For 2025-2026 Ballotpedia lists her on the Appropriations and Finance, Commerce and Economic Development, and Health and Human Services committees, the last as vice chair.

Herndon said her campaign priorities include affordable health care, including access to reproductive health care and mental health treatment, affordable housing, and policies on safe storage of firearms.
